heard: Astronomers cataloged a faint violet speck, assuming it was an ordinary star. In reality, TON-618 was an ultramassive black hole powered by a quasar 10.8 billion light-years away. Its event horizon radius spans approximately 1,300 astronomical units, swallowing the scale of our solar system. Gas whipping around its core exceeds orbital speeds of 10,000 kilometers per second. That infalling material unleashes a brilliance equal to 140 trillion suns, completely drowning out its host galaxy. Early measurements estimated 66 billion solar masses, later revised to roughly 40.7 billion suns. Surrounding it all is an enormous liminalpha gas nebula, spanning at least 100 kiloparsecs across. No singular monster in the cosmos has ever hidden behind such a quiet disguise.
